title: Extension by zero on a localized site is exact
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a Grothendieck site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $W$ be an object. Give $\mathcal C/W$ the localized topology, with coverings whose underlying families cover in $\mathcal C$. For the abelian sheaf categories [def-sp-abelian], the extension-by-zero functor $j_{W!}:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C/W)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is exact: for every short exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$ on $\mathcal C/W$, the sequence $0\to j_{W!}F_1\to j_{W!}F_2\to j_{W!}F_3\to0$ is exact on $\mathcal C$.

proof.text: Use the presheaf construction of [def-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. It is additive, and for a morphism alpha its presheaf-level map is the direct sum, over all maps V \to W, of the corresponding component maps of alpha.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Section 03DH and Lemma 03DJ, proof: construction of j_{U!}

proof.text: If alpha:F_1 \to F_2 is a monomorphism of abelian sheaves on C/W, then its underlying presheaf morphism has sectionwise injective components: the sheaf inclusion preserves kernels, so the kernel is the sectionwise kernel by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], and evaluation of presheaves is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact]. Therefore, at each V, the direct-sum map (j_{W,p!}alpha)_V is injective, since a finite-support element in its kernel has each component in the kernel of an injective alpha_{(V \to W)}.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), proof: the displayed direct-sum map on sections

proof.text: The presheaf map in Step 2 has zero kernel. Sheafification preserves finite limits, in particular kernels, by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Hence its sheafification j_{W!}alpha has zero kernel and is a monomorphism in Ab(C).

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DJ, proof: sheafification is exact

proof.text: For a short exact sequence 0 \to F_1 \to F_2 \to F_3 \to 0, the last map F_2 \to F_3 is a cokernel of the first by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel]. The functor F \mapsto (j_{W,p!}F)^\# of Steps 1-3 is left adjoint to restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint], so it preserves this cokernel by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Thus (j_{W,p!}F_2)^\# \to (j_{W,p!}F_3)^\# is a cokernel of (j_{W,p!}F_1)^\# \to (j_{W,p!}F_2)^\#.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), proof: right exactness from the adjunction

proof.text: The first map (j_{W,p!}F_1)^\# \to (j_{W,p!}F_2)^\# is monic by Steps 2-3, and the second is its cokernel by Step 4. The abelian-category criterion [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] therefore gives a short exact sequence 0 \to (j_{W,p!}F_1)^\# \to (j_{W,p!}F_2)^\# \to (j_{W,p!}F_3)^\# \to 0. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-adjunction], both F \mapsto (j_{W,p!}F)^\# and j_{W!} are left adjoint to j_W^*, so they are naturally isomorphic (uniqueness of adjoints); a sequence isomorphic to a short exact sequence is short exact, so 0 \to j_{W!}F_1 \to j_{W!}F_2 \to j_{W!}F_3 \to 0 is exact.

proof_origin.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact) and its proof
